text:
Jia: Heads-up — saw inconsistent completions on the prod canary when prefetch crosses a shard boundary right after a lease revoke. Repro steps + short log below.

Matt: Repro steps? can you paste the minimal trace we can run locally?

Jia: Steps: 1) send long prefix-heavy request that touches keyspace A..M (owned by shard-1) and N..Z (shard-2) 2) trigger eviction on shard-1 (low mem) 3) orchestrated rebalance revokes shard-1 lease mid-prefetch 4) completion sometimes contains stale token from old prefix cache -> wrong next-token. Log: 
```
2026-02-12T14:03:12Z prefetcher: starting prefetch keys=[kA..kM] target=shard-1 lease=lease_42
2026-02-12T14:03:12Z lease-agent: revoke lease=lease_42 -> lease_43 (reassign)
2026-02-12T14:03:12Z prefetcher: write_kv key=kX lease_stamped=lease_42
2026-02-12T14:03:12Z rpc: handoff complete -> shard-2 accepted keys kX..kZ
2026-02-12T14:03:12Z runtime: serve request id=... used_kv=kX (lease mismatch) -> incorrect token emitted
```

Devin: my guess: prefetch writes don't validate the current lease before persisting to the shared slab. If lease changes right after write but before handoff, target may read an entry that looks valid but is stale. Quick fix: stamp entries with lease_epoch and validate on read.

Katherine: Even with stamp+read-validate there's a race: the writer could stamp with old epoch and handoff so target sees a valid (but old) epoch that still matches its own view until it updates. We need either: a) write-check during persist that compares against a lease registry + CAS, or b) a revocation-phase that invalidates outstanding prefetches.

Sam: Both a) and b) have perf tradeoffs. Adding a CAS on every prefetch persist could add an extra RPC to lease service. What perf hit are we comfortable with?

Devin: Minimal change I can prototype: include lease_epoch in entries and the target read path rejects entries whose epoch != current_owner_epoch. That avoids CAS at write time. If mismatch -> treat as miss and fallback to normal read path. Pseudocode: 
```
// on read:
entry = slab.get(k)
if entry.lease_epoch != lease_manager.current_epoch(shard) {
  metric.inc("prefetch_epoch_mismatch")
  return MISS
}
return entry.value
```

Jia: That seems low-friction. But we need to ensure we get low false-negatives: a transient mismatch could increase read latency as we miss and re-serve. Plan: accept short-term perf regression, measure. I'll draft a canary job that simulates cross-shard prefixes and counts epoch_mismatch rate + end-to-end completion errors.

Matt: Back-compat note: existing slab entries have no epoch field. We'll have to treat missing epoch as epoch=0. That means after deploy there will be a window where old entries might be rejected. We should sweep/evict old entries or accept the miss. Which is less risky?

Katherine: Another option: on lease revoke owner can publish a prefetch-invalidate tombstone for keys it seeded. That is a more proactive invalidation but adds N RPCs on revoke and complexity around idempotency. Could batch tombstones per-prefix though.

Sam: Long-term, seems like we want an atomic prefetch handshake: owner sequences a prefetch intent, once target acknowledges, owner hands off. That would require a small sequencer service or extend lease-agent API. Might be a bigger refactor but it'd be safe.

Jia: Proposal: short-term = lease_epoch tagging + read-time reject + canary/metrics. Long-term = RFC for prefetch-handshake (owner -> sequencer -> target) and optionally a revoke-invalidate optimisation. I'll open a short PR for the epoch tag + read-check and a follow-up RFC doc for the handshake.

Devin: I can prototype the PR (low-risk flags + feature gate). Will measure p50/p95 request latency and epoch_mismatch counters. If mismatch rate is <0.1% and does not spike p95 beyond SLO, we roll.

Katherine: I'll draft the RFC layout: problem statement, handshake sketch, API surface, backwards compat, and perf cost model.

Matt: I'll own the canary: synthetic cross-shard workload + traffic shadow for 24h. Will monitor correctness regression + token error rate.

deploy-bot: canary job started: job/id=canary-cross-shard-prefetch-1995

Sam: :thumbsup: sounds pragmatic. Keep me posted if we need to block rebalances temporarily.

Jia: Thanks everyone. I'll add the PR link once Devin pushes. :slightly_smiling_face:
